headline: No shared execution or data path is documented; the main residual risk is low-probability prompt/cascade issues from manual handoff, while data leakage and capability conflict are blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable docs-only list with no I/O surfaces, and agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP bridge. That makes automated injection pathways absent, but a manual copy-paste handoff could still carry malicious text from A into B. The pairwise risk is therefore low, not none, because the only plausible bridge is human-mediated.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from agent A into agent B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is introduced, the pathway changes from manual to automated.
mitigations: Use a plain-text paste buffer and strip formatting before transfer.
Require the operator to summarize A's output in their own words before sending to B.
Disable any future shared clipboard or queue integration.
Add a one-line provenance note to copied snippets.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no network egress; agent B also touches no data classes and cannot read files, write files, or call APIs. With no shared workspace or outbound channel documented, there is no plausible data leakage path between them in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage analysis must be revisited.
IF agent B gains file-reading or API-calling capability, the current no-leak conclusion no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared storage.
Verify B remains fileless and API-less in deployment.
Document that A has no data inputs beyond static docs.
Run a quick permission audit before pairing.
requires-engineering: add automated policy checks for shared data paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces; agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Because neither agent can mutate a shared resource, there is no capability overlap that can produce write-write conflict.
conditions: IF agent A becomes runnable with write access to a shared directory, conflict risk would need reassessment.
IF agent B is granted filesystem or git write permissions, overlapping mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep A non-runnable in production.
Do not grant B write permissions.
Separate any future mutable resources by directory or repo.
Check that no orchestrator adds implicit locking assumptions.
requires-engineering: introduce explicit resource locks if writes are added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a static resource list, not an action-taking model, and agent B has no APIs, shell, or subprocesses to execute downstream actions. The main remaining pathway is human over-trust: an operator could treat A's curated content as authoritative and pass it into B without verification. That is a limited cascade, so low severity fits.
conditions: IF an operator uses A's list as authoritative input to B without checking sources, cascade risk increases.
IF B is later connected to action-taking tools, the blast radius expands beyond low.
mitigations: Require source verification before forwarding A's content.
Have B label A-derived claims as unverified.
Use a checklist for any human handoff between agents.
Limit B to drafting, not executing, responses.
requires-engineering: add citation validation before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress or data handling scopes that would create residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch. Because the pair does not process PHI, EU PII, or secrets in the provided profiles, there is no documented compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes, compliance review must be repeated.
IF retention or residency policies are added outside these profiles, the current conclusion no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Record that neither agent has secrets-handling scopes.
Review residency and retention policies before any deployment change.
Maintain a short data-class inventory.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
